- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model often underestimates downside risk; add downward buffer or adjust for volatility spike.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (especially days 1–5), especially when sentiment is neutral or positive — apply early correction by 5–10%.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast slope after spike, or add mean-reversion term.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (±0.3–0.7), model exhibits erratic behavior — use smoother interpolation or sentiment-weighted average for forecast adjustment.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion toward prior 5–10 day average, model tends to ignore it — incorporate 5-day moving average as baseline for correction.
- Forecast horizon 1–5 days: model is too optimistic; reduce forecast by 3–5% relative to 7–10 day average.
- Forecast horizon 6–10 days: model often overestimates — apply 2–4% downward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- Forecast horizon 11–30 days: model tends to underestimate — add 1–3% upward adjustment if sentiment is positive or volatile.
